text:
Sam Reinhart reached 700 career points on Nov. 14 in St. Louis, capping the night with what NHL.com and others called a highlight goal. It fit his month. He has 12 goals and 22 points in 23 games for Florida, six goals and 12 points in his last ten.

The best part is the process. Reinhart has 13.4 expected goals (the quality of his chances), 1.74 per 60 minutes, up from 1.28 last season. Only 12 goals on those looks means his own finishing is, if anything, a little behind. He is shooting a lot (72 shots) from places that score.

The caution sits around him. Florida has scored 8.2 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which is padding his points, and the Panthers have been outchanced at five-on-five with him out there (46.7% of the expected goals). That on-ice luck fades.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows why the chances keep coming: 1.8 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net, the most dangerous kind. A two-time Cup winner who finds the soft ice. Watch whether the line's five-on-five play catches up to the scoreboard.
headline: Reinhart keeps getting to the net
